title: All Sports Competition (Cornell University)
summary: All Sports Championship at Cornell University is an intramural program awarding the All Sports Trophy based on performance across Fall and Spring Term competitions. Points are earned per sport, with each concluding in a University Championship. Historically open to all students, the competition has seen periods of intense inter-fraternity rivalry, wartime suspension and military integration, and post-war oligarchic distribution among houses. The program originated in 1905 with Charles Van Patten 'Tar' Young's advocacy and expanded significantly by 1937, becoming the largest collegiate intramural program in the country.

mechanisms.title: Point accumulation across sports
mechanisms.explanation: Each sport competition ends in a University Championship, and the resulting points are tallied toward the All Sports Trophy. The trophy is awarded based on cumulative performance across the series of Fall and Spring Term sports.

mechanisms.title: Fraternal and organizational participation
mechanisms.explanation: Competition primarily involves fraternities, clubs, and informal student groupings. Historical data shows houses such as Beta Theta Pi, Chi Psi, and Sigma Alpha Epsilon achieving repeated victories, while the trophy has moved frequently among a wide competitor base in the program's early decades.
